title: Champion vs native Ascend aclnn (CANN 9.0.0), measured 2026-11-07

protocol.pypto_side: frozen remote_harness.py, latency_us = median per-round effective_us (PYPTO_BENCH=1)
protocol.aclnn_side: tools/aclnn_bench.py (pyacl + ctypes on libopapi.so): wall-clock per round (enqueue + acl.rt.synchronize_stream), median; executor fetched once and reused. Both sides end-to-end wall clock including host dispatch.
protocol.shape_policy: m-tier shape {M:4096, N:4096} (domain contract: q int8 [M,N], scale fp32 [M,1], x fp32)

aclnn_baseline_semantics: No single aclnn op performs per-token int8 dequant with a [M,1] fp32 scale at this contract, so the native baseline is the unfused decomposition aclnnCast(int8->fp32) + aclnnMul(broadcast scale [M,1]) — two global-memory round-trips, matching the two-pass decomposition the domain's own baseline encodes.
convention: speedup_pypto_vs_aclnn = aclnn_us / pypto_us; >1 means the pypto champion is faster
